argument: Pressure must change the production geometry of the entire sheet: several polygon bodies, the aperture, and the shared cut horizon must move together. A local dot or opacity change is not material agency.

With labels, readout, controls, captions, and furniture hidden, the first encounter should read as one dense construction body with a real absence, not as a route, card wall, or theatre. After pressure, the displaced silhouette and moved aperture must be findable in the body itself.

A short tap must be refused. A sustained press, the deterministic control, Enter, and Space must commit equivalent structural pressure; Delete must restore the exact previous sheet and R must release all memory.
v025 must break v022's slot occupancy, v023's temporal route, and v024's plane/shadow theatre through an object-sized paper body, a duration-bearing press, and a global negative-space rule.

Delete v025 if the pressure only opens a decorative hole, if the fragments keep their old geometry, if a short tap writes, if later cuts ignore the inherited aperture, or if the blind image needs the caption to be seen as one body rather than a collection of tiles.
